ADAPTIVE LOCAL RELIABILITY DESIGN FROM RETAINED PRODUCT EVIDENCE
Working result; no novelty or priority claim. Ordinary baseline included.

Scope
-----
Unknown independent Bernoulli primitive sources. A fixed read-once hierarchy
has four children at each internal node. Each node may assign the distinguished
weight-two role to any one child; the other three children have weight one;
the threshold is three. The allowed design family has 4^G elements for G gates.
This does not optimize arbitrary graph topology, overlapping subcircuits,
component replacement under arbitrary costs, or dependencies among sources.

The central useful task is selecting a better local role assignment from
retained evidence. Its confidence certificate can need far less acquisition
than estimating the full root reliability. Every construction and maintenance
operation is also available to an ordinary product-count estimator. There is
no demonstrated cached-restoration advantage here.

1. Exact swap identity and recursive optimization
------------------------------------------------
At a weighted-threshold node, give reliabilities p_a,p_b to weights w_a>=w_b.
Let S be the total score of the remaining independent children. Compare this
assignment to exchanging the two children. The exact difference is

  q_ab - q_ba
    = (p_a-p_b) Pr(theta-w_a <= S < theta-w_b).

Proof: the two assignments differ only when exactly one of the two children
succeeds. Their probability difference is p_a-p_b, multiplied by the difference
between the two threshold indicators. The latter is the displayed interval
indicator. Thus sorting child reliabilities in the same order as the weights
is optimal by successive interchange. Strictness requires both p_a>p_b and
positive probability for the pivotal interval. Some different weights can be
equivalent if no other-child score lies in that interval.

For the four-majority gate, with distinguished child j,

  g_j(q) = q_j [1-product_(i!=j)(1-q_i)]
             +(1-q_j) product_(i!=j)q_i.

Exchanging distinguished child a with ordinary child b gives

  g_a(q)-g_b(q) = (q_a-q_b)(q_c+q_d-2q_c q_d).

The second factor is Pr(child c != child d), strictly positive for full-support
child probabilities. The best distinguished child therefore has the largest
reliability, with ties harmless.

P1 COMPUTATIONAL REUSE BOUNDARIES — WORKING DERIVATIONS

Scope: local mathematical analysis and executable checks only. No external
writes, uploads, purchases, new helpers, or integration. Results below do not
claim priority. The conditional result depends on an unproved conjecture.

1. A FINITE COUNTEREXAMPLE TO FULL ADAPTIVE OPTIMALITY OF FIXED-BATCH DP

Let S,A,B be independent unknown probabilities with Beta(1/2,1/2) priors.
The scientific target is the read-once Boolean multiplexer mean

  theta = S A + (1-S) B.

Each observation is a fresh Bernoulli observation of one chosen probability.
The Bayes estimator is the posterior target mean; loss is squared error.
There are two observations available.

The prior variance of each probability is 1/8. The exact multilinear
variance formula gives

  Var(theta) = (1/4+1/8)(1/8+1/8) = 3/32 = 24/256.

All fixed allocations (order does not matter) have learned-mean variances:

  S,S: 0
  S,A or S,B: 5/256
  A,A or B,B: 1/48
  A,B: 1/32 = 8/256.

Hence the optimal fixed batch observes A and B once and has Bayes risk
24/256-8/256 = 16/256 = 1/16.

An adaptive policy first observes S. If that observation is one, it observes
A; if zero, it observes B. Each of the four two-observation transcripts has
probability 1/4. The final posterior target mean is 5/16 or 11/16, each with
probability 1/2. Its learned-mean variance is 9/256 and Bayes risk 15/256.
This is a 6.25% reduction of Bayes risk, or a 12.5% increase in learned
variance, relative to the exact best fixed batch. The gain is strict with
ordinary full-support positive Beta priors, without a limiting argument.

The exact script enumerates all 27 deterministic depth-two policies:
three first actions and three possible second actions after each first
outcome. It verifies this adaptive policy is globally optimal at budget two,
including all repeated-source choices. Randomizing policies cannot improve
their maximum because the expected gain is linear in the mixture.

More generally, for independent Beta(a,a) priors and s=2a,

  best fixed gain = 1/[8(s+1)^2],
  selector-first adaptive gain = (s+2)^2/[16(s+1)^4].

The latter is better for s<sqrt(2), i.e. a<1/sqrt(2).
This does not invalidate the proposed fixed-batch theorem. Independent fixed
experiments in disjoint subtrees produce independent posterior child means;
adaptive cross-subtree budget allocation destroys that

P1: COMPILING THE VALUE OF EXPERIMENTS
Retained inference representations, conditional Bayes risk, and adaptive planning
Working scientific result, 2026-10-31 branch

STATUS

This document gives proved identities, constructive algorithms, numerical
certificates, executed checks, and failures. It does not establish historical
priority, a general-purpose inference breakthrough, or practical superiority
over an equally equipped ordinary incremental method. The central algebra is
the centered-product / ANOVA variance identity. The proposed contribution is
the explicit experiment interface and its constructive, maintained optimization
compiler, with the statistical and numerical contracts kept intact.

The scientific question is now: given evidence about uncertain primitive
reliabilities, can retained computation determine which next experiments most
reduce uncertainty in a specified system property? The objective is useful
inference, rather than the number of repaired or generated sample bits.

The main positive result is an exact fixed-batch Bayes-risk optimizer on a
supplied read-once multiaffine tree. For bounded arity and a two-observation
budget it has linear construction and storage, ancestor-path updates, and
explicit recovered experiment choices. A second result solves the genuinely
adaptive two-observation problem in O(n h) arithmetic for bounded arity using
the same representation. Ordinary reversible hypothetical updates attain the
same adaptive complexity; that comparator is implemented and checked.

The broad structural principle is that fixed independent experiments compose
through their explained covariance on the target's feature space. A single
learned-variance number is sufficient for a scalar multiaffine interface.
Matrices are needed for multiple features, and adaptive continuation can need
more than either fixed-experiment scalar variance or a scalar budget profile.
The precise positive and negative statements follow below.

1. THE SCIENTIFIC CONTRACT AND THE COMPLETE RECORD

There are n stationary primitive sources. Conditional on p=(p_1,...,p_n), a
call to source i returns an independent Bernoulli(p_i) bit. Calling a source
does not produce a new system trajectory, and reusing a numerical circuit
does not acquire additional physical evidence. All calls are counted.
